title: HyperAid: Denoising in Hyperbolic Spaces for Tree-fitting and Hierarchical Clustering

problem.claim: Fit tree-metrics to data for hierarchical clustering and related applications.

gap.claim: It is unclear how to fit tree-metrics to noisy data that differs from tree structure, which causes poor performance, negative edge weights, and uncertainty about the best approximation objective.

contributions.claim: HyperAid denoises tree-metric data in hyperbolic spaces to make it more tree-like according to Gromov's δ hyperbolicity.
The paper conducts an ablation study comparing lp-norm and Dasgupta-loss approximation objectives.
The paper integrates HyperAid with schemes that enforce nonnegative edge weights.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe HyperAid as a new approach to tree-metric denoising in hyperbolic spaces.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HyperAid outperforms Neighbor Joining, TreeRep, and T-REX on synthetic and real-world data.
On the listed synthetic and real-world datasets, the authors report an average improvement of 125.94% relative to Neighbor Joining.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tree-metric fitting is important for hierarchical clustering and several application areas.
The noisy tree-metric fitting problem is less understood, with poor existing performance and negative edge weights.
The suitable approximation objective for noisy fitting is unknown.
HyperAid denoises data in hyperbolic spaces, compares approximation objectives, and supports nonnegative edge-weight enforcement.
The authors report improvements over existing methods on synthetic and real-world datasets, including a 125.94% average improvement over Neighbor Joining.

source_observation.claim: Transforming noisy data into a more tree-like representation is presented as a route to improved tree-metric fitting.

interpretation.claim: Representation denoising may be a useful intermediate step before applying hierarchical or tree-fitting methods.

application.claim: Consider geometry-aware preprocessing when fitting hierarchical structures to noisy relational data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when hyperbolic denoising is preferable to other preprocessing strategies.

source_observation.claim: The paper compares lp-norm and Dasgupta-loss objectives and integrates nonnegative edge-weight enforcement.

interpretation.claim: Objective selection and structural constraints can materially shape noisy hierarchical fitting.

application.claim: Evaluate multiple fitting objectives and enforce domain-relevant structural constraints when designing noisy tree-fitting pipelines.

exception.claim: The abstract does not report which objective or constraint combination is best across datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithmic details, hyperbolic-space configuration, or computational complexity of HyperAid.
The abstract does not provide per-dataset results, evaluation protocols, statistical uncertainty, or independent verification.
